newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan raises forward cover fee on forex deposit.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan raises forward cover fee on forex deposit.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan on Monday raised forward cover fee on foreign currency deposits placed with it by commercial banks amid fears of a possible marginal rupee devaluation.
The fee is charged by the SBP for providing exchange risk cover on deposits brought by banks from abroad.
An SBP official said the forward cover fee for dollar deposits had been raised to 5.0 percent per annum from 4.75 percent fixed on April 21, 1996 and for sterling to 4.37 percent from 4.04 percent.
Forward cover fee for mark deposits was raised to 7.20 percent from 6.66 percent and for yen deposits to 9.65 percent from 9.13 percent per annum, he said.
"The revised rates of fee will be applicable to deposits accepted/renewed/rolled over on or after 31st March," he said.

SBP did not say why the fee has been raised but bankers said the move might be related to a recent statement by the Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz in which he hinted at the possibility of a marginal devaluation of the rupee.
Aziz told the National Assembly on Thursday that a marginal devaluation was on cards.
"Some adjustment would be done whereby some marginal devaluation of the rupee would be inevitable to stabilise the national economy," he said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange's 100-share index tumbled 21.43 points, or 1.35 percent, to close at 1,569.87 on Monday on what dealers described as fears of a devaluation of the rupee against the dollar.
"Investors fear devaluation of rupee," dealer Shakil Anwar said. "The sentiment was weak because past devaluations did not help Pakistan to boost its exports."
The SBP rate, last changed on October 22, was unchanged at 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar. The rupee depreciated by 17.86 percent against the dollar in 1996.
